title: PM2.5 Exposure, Obesity, and Cardiovascular Health
official: Investigating Interactions Between PM2.5 Exposure, Obesity, Cardiovascular Health and Dietary Antioxidant in Subjects With Obesity
summary: Obesity and exposure to fine particulate matter (particles of aerodynamic diameter less than 2.5 µm, PM2.5) air pollution are established risk factors for cardiovascular (CV) morbidity and mortality. This proposed pilot project seeks to assess interactions between PM2.5 exposure, obesity, CV health, and dietary antioxidant in subjects with obesity.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* ≥21 years old
* diagnosis of hypertension (BP ≥140/90 mm Hg)
* obesity (BMI\>30)

Exclusion Criteria:

* any CV event (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure) in the past 3 months
* unstable CV condition (class 3-4 angina or heart failure) or any medical condition that would place the subject at risk from participation or jeopardize study integrity (per investigators)
* expected overnight travel outside their home during the 9-week study period
* unable to comprehend/sign informed consent
* lung disease requiring oxygen
* cancer receiving active treatment or chemotherapy
* CPAP use for sleep apnea
* CV medication change in the prior month
